# Dual run of test/x86/probe/vga_census.asm, 2026-10-16, same 512-byte boot
# sector on both models:
#
#   cemu  --machine x86 --isa x86 vga_census.bin
#   qemu-system-i386 -drive file=vga_census.bin,format=raw,if=ide,index=0 -boot c \
#       -display none -serial file:... -no-reboot \
#       -device isa-debug-exit,iobase=0xf4,iosize=0x4
#
# The suite cell compares cemu's live transcript against the `cemu` line below;
# the `qemu` line is what the reference card answered for the same sector.
# Exit: debug-exit value 11 -> status 23 on both.
cemu census 
qemu census 

60 register reads walked (CRTC 0x00-0x11, graphics 0x00-0x0F, sequencer
0x00-0x07, attribute 0x00-0x11) plus five deterministic cases. **Two fields
differ, and neither is a card difference:**

  - `C0E00` / `C0F00` against QEMU's `C0E02` / `C0F80` — CRTC R14/R15 are the
    cursor *position*, written by the firmware's own text output
    (`stdvga.c:301 stdvga_set_cursor_pos`). The two models printed different
    numbers of characters before the guest started, so the cursor sits
    elsewhere. Registered as not-a-bug in 片 30, and it is the same story here.
  - Everything else is byte-identical, **including all 18 attribute-controller
    reads.**

That last line is a correction, and it is the reason this file exists in this
shape. An earlier copy of this probe carried

    in al, 0x3da                 ; reset the attribute flip-flop

which NASM cannot encode — `in al, imm8` is the 8-bit port form, and the
16-bit port silently truncates to 0xDA (nasm warns: "byte data exceeds bounds").
The flip-flop was therefore never reset on either model, the attribute walk read
the index latch instead of the registers, and the 13 "attribute controller
read-back differences" recorded from it were a probe artifact, not evidence
about the card. Fixed to the DX form, the walk agrees with the reference card on
every ATC register. The decode-model difference this card *does* take from
IBM VGA TR is measured in the sibling probe instead: see
`vga_readback_qemu.txt`, one field.
